## Overview

Add opt-in sharing of unfinished NIXL prefix loads across requests with separate producer leases, following [RFC #59141](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59141) and dependent on [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418).

Candidate `376f6836` incorporates parent `acc2479` and main snapshot `fcae5c98`. [NIXL-only comparison (16 files)](https://github.com/NolenLiang/vllm/compare/3ede47677ab1c43a6f79d1a0926e1b9b6a876378...376f6836b497b59ce556b24c568683a9773ce235); the full PR against main also includes the unmerged parent. Draft pending human review and personal test execution of this adaptation.

## Claims

- Concurrent consumers of the same leased physical producer prefix can share immutable complete destination blocks while retaining private writable tails. Each sibling has its own producer lease; matching tokens alone is insufficient.
- Followers release unused leases without another READ. Cancellation retains owner destinations and heartbeat until terminal transfer status; failures follow the parent's recompute/fail policy without rereading released follower leases.
- The rebased integration preserves the NIXL attachment callback and uses the parent's single queue removal/KV-holding transition. Existing tests now check stage counts through cancellation/completion and both receive-failure policies.

## Validation

**Current source:** `376f6836b497b59ce556b24c568683a9773ce235`, tree `8b25c9e4793edb09ba90aec15e2293ee1c344fa0`. Published tracked files match the tested tree.

| Focused selection | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| Remote-prefill lifecycle and NIXL heartbeat | 109 |
| Offloading scheduler, prefix caching, KV-load recovery, admission | 649 |
| NIXL worker receive/polling/failure/handshake | 30 |
| Selected HMA scheduler cases | 2 |
| **Distinct total** | **790** |

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed on 19 files, including the current Python 3.11-target mypy hook. Whitespace checks passed. [Exact test commands, logs and environment details](https://github.com/NolenLiang/vllm/blob/c4f6bfdd11c2718f767b85c82ed2af8314dd8135/pr-rebase-evidence/20261011/README.md).

Execution used WSL2 x86_64, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu132 and reused installed native extensions whose build provenance was not re-established. Focused regressions use mocked transport boundaries; this is not actual NIXL peer-transfer or model-output acceptance testing.

**Historical GPU evidence remains tied to its tested source.** Candidate `e6e362a` recorded 186 compute-test passes and 12 actual peer-failure trials (recompute/fail × 16384/16385-token prompts × three repetitions). Event replay checked native in-progress status around peer termination, disconnect, release, core failure propagation, destination reclamation and recovery on the same D process after restarting P.

The same candidate's untraced off/on/on/off comparison used Qwen3-0.6B, two GB200 GPUs on one aarch64 node, TP1/PP1, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0 and NIXL 1.4.1: 120 measured groups, 520 D requests and 64 correctness outputs. Text/finish reasons matched; maximum token-logprob error was 0.00709399 against 0.01 tolerance. At four siblings, 4096/4097-token cells changed four transfers to one and reduced payload by 75%; eight-sibling median payload was unchanged with ordinary prefix caching. Timing drift prevents a stable latency claim. This is GRPO-shaped serving, not trainer integration; payload is connector telemetry, not NIC wire bytes.

Earlier snapshots separately recorded cancellation, real-in-progress polling-exception and heartbeat-crossing probes with native background progress disabled. Those do not establish final-source coverage. The former dual-GB200 environment is no longer accessible. Final-source GPU lifecycle/model-output validation and default-progress heartbeat-crossing evidence remain outstanding. Earlier upstream pre-commit did not execute after contributor-eligibility precheck failure; local checks are separate from upstream CI and no new upstream success is claimed.

## Details

Initial scope is direct GPU pull, TP1/PP1/CP1, one full-attention cache group and prefix caching, enabled with `enable_shared_prefix_loads=true` and disabled by default. Unsupported layouts or missing producer block geometry retain independent loads. The owner keeps its full READ; followers share only complete prefix blocks before the last request token.

The parent supplies allocation, reference counting and failure propagation. NIXL adds producer/endpoint/geometry/physical-block compatibility and lease coordination. HTTP rejection cleanup tracks successful admission across child tasks. Unknown polling exceptions retain native handles; typed remote disconnect enters release, and a failed release retains the handle and blocks. Persistent unobservable native status does not promise bounded recovery.

This refresh addresses the parent's KV-holding queue and KV-fetch tracking changes. Keeping both the old pop and the parent's `skip_request` would remove a second waiting request or access an empty queue. The adaptation keeps the callback but lets the parent perform the transition once.

Before initial submission, open-PR searches found no competing #59141 implementation. [#55374](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55374) composes Store/NIXL ranges within one request; [#43509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43509) handles best-of fan-out/early notifications. This follow-up shares an unfinished READ across distinct producer leases.

@@ -132,6 +132,35 @@ python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py \
     - In bidirectional mode, the decoder caches KV blocks for multi-turn conversations. This TTL controls how long those blocks are held before being released. Unlike the prefiller lease, this TTL is not renewed via heartbeats.
     - Example: `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector_extra_config": {"decoder_kv_blocks_ttl": 600}}'`
 
+## Sharing an In-Flight Prefix Load
+
+The pull connector can let compatible requests wait for one in-flight read of
+their common prefix. Enable it on the decoder with
+`"enable_shared_prefix_loads": true` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, together
+with prefix caching. It is disabled by default.
+
+The initial supported configuration is full attention with one KV cache group,
+TP1, PP1, no context parallelism, no speculative decoding, no host staging,
+and no bidirectional transfer. Each decoder request must carry its own producer
+request and lease. A single producer lease cannot be fanned out to multiple
+decoder requests using this option.
+
+Sharing requires matching local prefix hashes (including cache salt), the same
+producer engine and endpoint, matching block sizes, and identical physical
+producer blocks for the shared prefix. The producer must return
+`remote_block_size` and `pcp_size`; older producers fall back to independent
+reads. Distinct producer requests can meet these conditions through producer prefix caching.
+Identical tokens in different producer blocks do not qualify, so a cold,
+concurrent producer batch may still require independent reads.
+
+The initiating request loads its entire prompt as usual. Followers share only
+complete prefix blocks and compute their own remaining tail locally (up to one
+block for an identical full prompt). Their unused producer leases are released
+through notification-only operations. Cancelling the initiating request keeps
+its read and lease alive until completion. A failed shared read follows
+`kv_load_failure_policy`; recomputation uses local compute, not the followers'
+already released producer leases.
+
 ## Bidirectional KV Transfer (Multi-turn)
 
 In standard disaggregated prefilling, KV cache flows in one direction: Prefill (P) computes the KV cache and Decode (D) reads from P. For multi-turn conversations this is wasteful — D already holds the KV cache corresponding to the generated tokens from prior turns, yet P must recompute it from scratch on every new turn. Bidirectional KV transfer lets P **pull** existing KV blocks from D via RDMA before computing only the new tokens, significantly reducing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for long-prefill such as **multi-turn heavy scenarios**.
